passage: I'm Shalini, and on Thursday I sat through a film society meeting that ran ninety minutes without a single agenda item. Yusuf spoke first, and he kept going: posters, a guest speaker, the hall booking, then posters again. Two juniors opened their mouths and closed them. Nobody took notes. When it ended, people simply stood up. In the corridor one person said the guest talk was cancelled, another said postponed, and someone else thought they'd been asked to book the hall. I had written "budget?" in my notebook and never got to ask it. Later I heard Yusuf tell someone the meeting had been really productive. I'm not sure he noticed how many of us left with different answers.

qa.q: How long did the film society meeting run?
qa.a: It ran ninety minutes without a single agenda item.

qa.q: What was Shalini feeling when Shalini wrote "budget?" in the notebook and never got to ask it?
qa.a: Frustrated and unheard, since the question never had a place in the meeting.

qa.q: What could the group do next time so everyone leaves with the same outcome?
qa.a: Send a short agenda beforehand, give each item a few minutes and write down the decisions before people leave.

qa.q: Why might Yusuf see the meeting differently from the others?
qa.a: Yusuf probably felt it was productive because he got to talk through many ideas, and did not notice people left with different memories.

grounding: Shows a participant watching a meeting with no agenda where one voice dominates and everyone leaves with a different outcome.

passage:
Monday. Rukmini, an intern, sat in a one-hour team meeting with no agenda. Payal, the loudest voice in the room, talked about the client, the website and the holiday rota, jumping between them, and the meeting ended when the lunch trolley arrived. Nobody said what had been decided.

Wednesday. Two team members had each started the same slide deck, and nobody had begun the client email. Rukmini had written "deck?" in her notebook on Monday and now saw why.

Friday. Payal asked, "Who is doing the email?" Three people gave three different answers about who had agreed to it. An hour was lost sorting it out, and Rukmini decided to keep a list of decisions and share it after every meeting.

qa.a: The lunch trolley arriving ended the meeting.

qa.q: What was Rukmini thinking on Wednesday when she saw the two slide decks?
qa.a: Rukmini understood why she had written "deck?" in her notebook, and probably felt frustrated at the wasted effort.

qa.q: What could Rukmini do after Friday's confusion?
qa.a: Keep a list of decisions and share it after each meeting so everyone has the same record.

qa.q: How might Payal have experienced the Monday meeting compared with the others?
qa.a: Payal probably felt it went smoothly because Payal did most of the talking, and did not notice that others left unsure of what was decided.

grounding: Shows an attendee living with the results of a meeting with no agenda, no record of decisions and different memories.
